text.p: Albanian soccer officials said on Friday the resumpion of the national league had been postponed until next week awaiting a government guarantee on security for players.
All matches have been cancelled since the end of January amid country-wide unrest and protests sparked by the collapse of several pyramid investment schemes.

"We are preparing to resume games next Wednesday and hope the Interior Ministry will give us a positive answer, by Monday at the latest," Eduard Dervishi, secretary general of the Albanian football association, told Reuters.
Officials, who are concerned that large gatherings of spectators could spark anti-government demonstrations, had originally hoped to restart games this weekend.

The government cancelled all sports events last month when mass protests began to spread around the contry but last Monday sports secretary of state Marjeta Zace told the soccer foundation to restart the national championships.
But Dervishi said no matches would be held this Saturday or Sunday, the fifth weekend in succession.
Tirana hopes Albania's World Cup group nine home qualifiers against Ukraine on March 29 and Germany on April 2 will go ahead but officials said they were still awaiting an answer from FIFA.
A friendly international against Macedonia had to be cancelled last week after the neighbouring country's authorities refused permission for the team to travel to Tirana.
